mcqs.question: A line touches a circle at point P. Which statement about the point of contact is correct?

options.A: It is the midpoint of the line segment joining the two points where the line intersects the circle.
options.B: It is the point where the line meets the circle and the radius drawn to it is perpendicular to the line.
options.C: It is always the farthest point of the circle from the line.
options.D: It coincides with the centre of the circle.

mcqs.answer: It is the point where the line meets the circle and the radius drawn to it is perpendicular to the line.
mcqs.explanation: The point of contact of a tangent is the unique point where the line touches the circle. At this point the radius drawn to the contact point is perpendicular to the tangent. Option A describes a property of a chord, not a tangent. Options C and D are false.

mcqs.question: Why is the radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent to a circle always perpendicular to the tangent line?

options.A: Because the radius is the longest line that can be drawn from the centre to any point on the circle.
options.B: Because the shortest distance from the centre to a straight line is measured along the perpendicular, and a tangent touches the circle at only one point.
options.C: Because the tangent line is a diameter of the circle.
options.D: Because the centre, point of contact, and any other point on the tangent are collinear.

mcqs.answer: Because the shortest distance from the centre to a straight line is measured along the perpendicular, and a tangent touches the circle at only one point.
mcqs.explanation: The distance from a point (the centre) to a line is minimum along the perpendicular. Since a tangent meets the circle at exactly one point, the radius to that point must be the shortest distance, hence perpendicular. Options A, C, and D are unrelated or incorrect.

mcqs.question: In which of the following situations can the tangent‑radius perpendicularity theorem be directly used to find a required length?

options.A: A tangent is drawn from an external point to a circle and the length of the tangent segment is required.
options.B: A secant cuts the circle at two points and the length of the chord is required.

mcqs.answer: A tangent is drawn from an external point to a circle and the length of the tangent segment is required.
mcqs.explanation: When a tangent is drawn from an external point, the radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent, allowing the use of the right‑triangle relationship to compute the tangent length. For a secant, the perpendicularity theorem does not apply directly. Hence only situation A uses the theorem.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a tangent from a secant of a circle?

options.A: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, whereas a secant intersects the circle at two distinct points.
options.B: A tangent always passes through the centre of the circle, while a secant never does.
options.C: A tangent is always longer than a secant drawn from the same external point.
options.D: A tangent and a secant are the same; the terms are interchangeable.

mcqs.answer: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, whereas a secant intersects the circle at two distinct points.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a tangent meets the circle at a single point; a secant cuts the circle at two points. Options B, C, and D are false statements.

mcqs.question: In the context of a circle, a tangent is best defined as:

options.A: A straight line that touches the circle at exactly one point.
options.B: A line that passes through the centre of the circle.
options.C: A curve that intersects the circle at two points.
options.D: A segment joining two points on the circle.

mcqs.answer: A straight line that touches the circle at exactly one point.
mcqs.explanation: The definition of a tangent to a circle is a straight line that meets the circle at precisely one point. The other options describe a diameter, a secant, and a chord respectively.

mcqs.question: The point at which a tangent meets a circle is called the:
mcqs.explanation: The unique point where a tangent touches the circle is termed the point of contact. The centre is unrelated, and the other options describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: The tangent‑radius perpendicularity theorem states that:

options.A: The radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent is parallel to the tangent line.
options.B: The radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent is perpendicular to the tangent line.
options.C: The tangent line bisects the radius of the circle.
options.D: The tangent and the radius form a 45° angle at the point of contact.

mcqs.answer: The radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent is perpendicular to the tangent line.
mcqs.explanation: The theorem explicitly says that the radius to the point where a tangent touches the circle is at right angles (90°) to the tangent. Options A, C, and D contradict the theorem.

mcqs.question: A circle has radius 5 cm. A tangent touches the circle at point P. What is the measure of the angle between OP (the radius) and the tangent line at P?
mcqs.explanation: By the tangent‑radius perpendicularity theorem, the radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, forming a right angle of 90°. The other angles are inconsistent with the theorem.
